The operator convention calls for a single DATE column over year/month/day, but this proposal's schema maps one source column to exactly one target and cannot combine three source columns into one derived date; year (distinct_count=1, value 2013.0), month (distinct_count=6, 1.0-6.0), and day (distinct_count=31, 1.0-31.0) are kept as separate required INTEGER columns pending a downstream combine step.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 166158, so no exact-duplicate dedupe pass is required for this table.

year, month, day, carrier_code, flight, and sched_dep_time are all required null_rate 0.0 columns that together plausibly identify one scheduled flight departure; tail_number and dep_time are excluded from the grain because they carry null_rate 0.009154 and 0.029388 respectively.

dep_time (null_rate 0.029388, 4883 nulls), arr_time (null_rate 0.0307, 5101 nulls), dep_delay_minutes, arr_delay_minutes (null_rate 0.032981, 5480 nulls), and air_time_minutes share nulls because, per operator context, a flight that never departed has no departure or arrival time; nulls are retained rather than imputed.

dep_delay, arr_delay, air_time, and distance are measures and are renamed to dep_delay_minutes, arr_delay_minutes, air_time_minutes, and distance_miles per the operator's convention of suffixing measures with their unit.

carrier, origin, and dest are code columns with 16, 3, and 100 distinct values respectively, renamed to carrier_code, origin_code, and destination_code per the operator's convention of naming code columns with a _code suffix and spelling out abbreviated names.
tailnum is renamed to tail_number per the operator's convention to spell out abbreviated column names; retained nullable because null_rate is 0.009154 (1521 nulls).

purpose: This silver table cleans the bronze nyc_flights capture of the nycflights13 flights table, covering January-June 2013 departures from JFK, LGA, and EWR, by typing timestamp and measure columns, applying the operator's naming conventions, and dropping Airbyte capture metadata, to feed downstream flight-delay and on-time-performance analysis.
usage: Consumers should join or group on the declared grain (year, month, day, carrier_code, flight, sched_dep_time) to identify one scheduled departure, and must treat nulls in dep_time, arr_time, dep_delay_minutes, arr_delay_minutes, air_time_minutes, and tail_number as flights that never departed or lack a recorded tail number rather than as missing data to impute.
limitations: year, month, and day remain three separate INTEGER columns rather than a single DATE column because this proposal's schema can only map one source column to one target and cannot combine three source columns into a derived date; dep_time, arr_time, dep_delay_minutes, arr_delay_minutes, and air_time_minutes retain nulls at rates between 2.9% and 3.3% for flights that never departed, and tail_number is null for 0.9% of rows; the grain has not been measured for uniqueness against the full warehouse table and must be validated before approval.
